BLOCK DISCOVERY Before designing a page, read get-theme-styles once: how the theme already draws text, headings, links and buttons. Set a size, colour or font on a block only where it should differ from that. List blocks before choosing one: list-blocks {source:"core"|"acf"|"registered"|"all",search?,page?,limit?}. All sources read the local server registry. "registered" means other providers, excluding core and ACF. Use the returned exact name with get-block-source {name}: it returns the schema, not source files. When it also returns guide, read it before writing that block: checked markup and behavior the schema does not show. list-blocks marks those blocks with guide:true. A JavaScript-only registration is not visible in the server registry. Do not invent its schema. list-block-usage {name} answers where a block stands: pages, posts, custom records, global blocks and templates, with a count each. Use it before changing the same block everywhere, not a text search of the content. SCHEMA AND SAVED CONTENT attributes contains the WordPress schema (including type, source, selector and default when declared). supports, parent and ancestor describe registration constraints. These are not a complete editor serializer. Follow writeMode. "markup" requires complete Gutenberg saved markup, with delimiters and InnerBlocks. A PHP render callback (dynamic:true) does NOT prove JavaScript save() returns null. The plugin does not execute save() or guarantee that arbitrary supplied markup passes editor validation. Reuse valid markup from get-content; verify by reopening the WordPress editor as well as the frontend. "attributes" allows a known save contract; "unsupported" means do not write that block through MCP. THEME SETTINGS (themeSettings) Only features the block supports are listed; an absent group cannot be set on this block. Use a preset by its slug: palette -> "textColor"/"backgroundColor": slug; gradientPresets -> "gradient": slug; fontSizes -> "fontSize": slug; fontFamilies -> "fontFamily": slug. spacingSizes -> style.spacing.padding|margin.: "var:preset|spacing|". shadow presets -> style.shadow: "var:preset|shadow|". A value outside the presets goes under style.* and only where the matching custom switch is true (custom, customGradient, customFontSize, customSpacingSize). styles -> put the variant's className on the block ("is-style-"); `sets` shows what the theme draws for it, isDefault marks the look without a class; align -> "align": one of the listed values; a variation is its attributes. SAVED MARKUP FOR THESE SETTINGS (writeMode "markup") The comment carries the attributes; the HTML must carry what the editor writes for them. When the site already has such a block, copy its shape from get-content. Otherwise: textColor:"S" -> classes has-S-color has-text-color. backgroundColor:"S" -> has-S-background-color has-background. fontSize:"S" -> has-S-font-size. fontFamily:"S" -> has-S-font-family. borderColor:"S" -> has-border-color has-S-border-color. A custom gradient (style.color.gradient) -> class has-background and inline background:. align:"wide"|"full"|"center" -> alignwide / alignfull / aligncenter. A style variation -> its className in the comment's className attribute AND in the class list (is-style-). Text alignment is style.typography.textAlign:"center" -> class has-text-align-center (not a textAlign attribute). A preset in style.* is written "var:preset|spacing|50" in the comment and var(--wp--preset--spacing--50) in the inline style (the same for |shadow|, |color|, |font-size|): style="margin-bottom:var(--wp--preset--spacing--50)". The editor writes inline declarations border first, then margin, then padding (top, right, bottom, left); style.spacing.blockGap writes no inline style at all. Example:

Title

The class goes on the block's own element, with exceptions: core/button puts colour, radius and shadow on the inner and the variation class on the outer div; core/image puts border and shadow on the and has-custom-border on the figure. The server checks the comment's attribute names against the schema; it does not check that classes match them. A wrong class is stored as sent and the editor then reports the block as invalid: reopen the editor after such a save. Void elements may be written either way (
